tasks.short: Apply authorised corrections and record omissions, errors and unresolved inconsistencies.

steps.what: Locate reported errors and their surrounding text in the current copy.
Choose justified corrections and separate issues requiring clarification.

loop.input: Anchored error context, approved copy and applicable style rules.
loop.output: Minimal proposed corrections and clarification questions.
loop.check: Validate anchors and protected figures; proofreader approves corrections and rejects unsupported additions.
loop.stop: One proposal and one repair per issue; unresolved intent becomes an open query.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contextual inconsistencies need language interpretation; exact mechanical replacements use rules.

steps.what: Apply approved corrections with tracked changes in the current copy.
Record corrections and unresolved issues in the proofing log.
Ask the copywriter to clarify omissions or inconsistencies affecting meaning.

tasks.design: Configure anchored corrections and tracked changes in the {DOCS}, with a correction log in the {PROJECT}. A bounded loop proposes contextual fixes for approval, while the {WORKFLOW} applies approved replacements and records their history; the proofreader handles questions about meaning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applying changes and updating the log were separate actions, while unclear omissions could not safely be filled automatically.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured annotations and revision controls can connect approved changes to their audit history. A bounded loop can draft minimal fixes without taking publication authority.
tasks.still_hard: An omitted fact needs an authoritative source. Concurrent edits, protected claims and unclear author intent require exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a correction would become an editorial or factual change requiring another person's decision.

ambition.what: Recurring error feedback for campaign writers.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into repetitive edits and duplicate logging. With an agreed remit, the proofreader can recommend targeted writing guidance from recurring error patterns.

reach.task: Turn recurring proofing errors into clearer editorial guidance.
reach.learn: Editorial boundaries, evidence sampling and useful feedback without rewriting the author's voice.

evidence.claim: Tracked changes and structured issue records can automate application and logging after approval.
Contextual correction proposals need local evaluation; the digest provides no documented proofreading outcome.

assumptions: The proofreader may apply minor corrections within a defined remit.
The baseline uses a shared proofing log in the {PROJECT}; some companies keep it in the {DOCS}.
Only approved replacements are applied; changed anchors stop the operation.
Time and build ranges are estimates and exclude duplicate savings from the marking task.
Access and any consultation under national rules must be confirmed locally.
unknowns: The boundary between permitted corrections and changes requiring editorial approval.
Whether the {DOCS} supports reliable tracked-change operations.
Whether correction records contain personal or confidential information.

How often do concurrent edits invalidate an approved correction?

Handle stale anchors and failed tracked-change operations.
Maintain protected terms and correction permissions.
Review recurring error patterns before issuing writing guidance.
tasks.statement: Correct or record omissions, errors, or inconsistencies found.

tasks.short: Mark spelling, grammar, punctuation, typography and layout errors in marketing proofs.

steps.what: Open the current proof, approved copy and style guide.
Check spelling, punctuation and typography; annotate mechanical errors.
Assess contextual grammar and punctuation; accept corrections or flag uncertainty.

loop.input: Versioned text segments, mechanical annotations and relevant style rules.
loop.output: Proposed language annotations with quoted spans and reasons.
loop.check: Validate quoted spans and rule references; proofreader approves annotations before handoff.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per segment; invalid or ambiguous suggestions return to the proofreader.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch mechanical patterns but cannot reliably judge contextual grammar or intended meaning.

steps.what: Inspect arrangement, line breaks and visual hierarchy; mark compositional errors.
Send the marked proof and correction instructions to the desktop publisher.

tasks.design: Configure the {DOCS} proof queue, dictionaries and style checks, then add a bounded language review loop for contextual suggestions. The proofreader approves language annotations and inspects composition; the {WORKFLOW} routes the versioned marked proof to the desktop publisher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing checks cover mechanics, while contextual errors and annotations across file versions require manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable checks, document anchors and bounded language review can be assembled with less implementation effort.
tasks.still_hard: Intentional language, multilingual nuance and visual composition remain difficult. Braille proofs need specialist validation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparent error expresses the intended voice, meaning or reading experience.

ambition.what: Preflight checks for campaign briefs before layout begins.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward contextual exceptions and composition checks. A delegated remit could let the proofreader return incomplete briefs before layout starts.

reach.task: Prevent text overflow and awkward line breaks in campaign layouts.
reach.learn: Layout constraints, typography and how template changes affect reading order.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling checks and bounded contextual suggestions are feasible; proofreading accuracy and time savings need local testing.
CHILI GraFx supports governed layout templates, which can prevent some recurring layout variation.

assumptions: The baseline is digital marketing proofs in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Step shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
Document work dominates; occasional email handoff does not imply a meeting-heavy task.
EU GDPR and AI Act obligations apply. Employee consultation depends on national rules and the proposed implementation.

Whether the style guide contains explicit, current rules.
Whether employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.

Maintain dictionaries, style rules and annotation anchors.
Sample accepted proofs for missed errors and unnecessary corrections.
tasks.statement: Mark copy to indicate and correct errors in type, arrangement, grammar, punctuation, or spelling, using standard printers' marks.

tasks.short: Verify that requested corrections appear in revised proofs without introducing new errors.

steps.what: Retrieve the marked proof, correction request and revised proof.
Compare each requested correction with the revised proof and record its status.
Inspect changed areas for reflow, displaced elements and newly introduced errors.
Approve the proofing pass or return outstanding corrections to the desktop publisher.

tasks.design: A deterministic comparison on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles correction identifiers and expected replacements against revised files in the {DOCS}. It produces a change map and exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}; the proofreader checks visual effects and approves the proof status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Corrections were embedded in annotations without stable identifiers or machine-readable expected results.
tasks.enabler_now: Version tracking, structured correction records and text or rendered-file comparisons support a small deterministic tool.
tasks.still_hard: Page reflow, outlined text and handwritten marks can break matching. A detected difference does not establish visual correctness.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing when a correctly applied correction damages the surrounding page or reading sequence.

ambition.what: Release each completed revision batch from proofing as soon as its checks pass.

tasks.altitude: Most rereading becomes targeted inspection of changes and exceptions. The proofreader can gain authority to close proofing batches within agreed release criteria.

reach.task: Validate revised layouts before returning proofs.
reach.learn: Text extraction limits, page reflow and reliable correction identifiers.

evidence.claim: Structured replacement instructions and document differences can be reconciled deterministically; visual acceptance still needs inspection.

assumptions: The future correction request records expected text or an explicit visual instruction.
Unsupported instructions become exceptions rather than being marked complete automatically.
Proof status is an internal quality decision; publication approval remains a separate action.
Time and build ranges are estimates. Work overlaps other supplied tasks and should not be counted twice.
Consent and access ranges assume routine access; consultation under national rules may extend them.
unknowns: Whether old and revised proofs have reliable version identifiers.
How often text is outlined, scanned or otherwise unavailable for extraction.
Who currently has authority to close a proofing pass.

Which visual instructions require direct human verification?
new_work: Resolve unmatched corrections and ambiguous version pairs.
Maintain extraction and comparison adapters.
Audit false completion flags and missed reflow effects.
tasks.statement: Read corrected copies or proofs to ensure that all corrections have been made.

tasks.short: Check marketing text and figures against approved source records and flag discrepancies.

steps.what: Identify the authoritative source and applicable version for each item being checked.
Retrieve source records and corresponding proof passages.
Compare names, figures, dates, units and wording; mark mismatches.
Clarify conflicting sources and distinguish errors from authorised differences.
Record confirmed discrepancies and supporting source references for correction.

tasks.design: Read-only connectors bring approved records from the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {ECOMMERCE} into a comparison job on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks preserve source references and flag mismatches using explicit locale and unit rules; the {WORKFLOW} collects clarification and generates a verification report without changing source records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proofs and source records lacked stable links, and manual checking hid differences in versions, units and formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Small connectors, explicit field mappings and deterministic comparison rules can now be built with less effort.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting sources and unsupported scans need human handling. Matching a source proves consistency, not the truth of a marketing claim.
tasks.human_edge: Establishing which source has authority and recognising when equal-looking figures have different meanings.

ambition.what: Cross-channel price and date consistency checks before campaign launch.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated comparisons toward source conflicts and unresolved discrepancies. The proofreader could gain authority to request a hold on inconsistent campaign items.

reach.task: Reconcile campaign prices and offer dates with web shop records.
reach.learn: Price validity, tax presentation, locale formats and promotion timing.

evidence.claim: Exact field and text comparisons can use deterministic rules without a language model.
Source authority and semantic equivalence still require judgement; no direct proofreading case is supplied.

The baseline sources include the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {ECOMMERCE}; actual connectors depend on the company's channels.
Digital text and structured records form the initial scope; unsupported inputs enter an exception queue.
The rule-heavy comparison justifies less model use than the judgement-heavy prior suggests.
Time and build ranges are estimates; access and consultation requirements depend on the local implementation.

How frequently do matching values conceal different units, periods or definitions?

Investigate conflicting records and unsupported inputs.
Monitor connector failures and stale snapshots.
Sample matches as well as discrepancies for missed semantic differences.
tasks.statement: Compare information or figures on one record against same data on other records, or with original copy, to detect errors.

tasks.short: Check disputed grammar and composition against references or a specialist reader.

steps.what: Isolate the disputed wording and identify the applicable language and house style.
Locate relevant entries in approved grammar references and the house style.
Compare the wording with reference guidance and note a supported correction.

loop.input: Disputed passage, surrounding text, and retrieved reference extracts with edition identifiers.
loop.output: A proposed correction, supporting quotation, and any conflicting guidance.
loop.check: Verify quotations against retrieved text and show the original passage beside the proposal for human review.
loop.stop: One proposal and one repair attempt; missing support or conflicting rules goes to the proofreader.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search finds rules, but applying them to context sometimes requires interpreting free text.

steps.what: Ask a specialist reader to resolve language questions that references leave uncertain.

tasks.design: Index licensed references and the house style in the {DOCS}, with exact lookup for defined spellings and terminology. A bounded reader proposes cited interpretations for unresolved passages; the proofreader reviews them and consults a specialist reader when guidance conflicts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference material was fragmented, and grammar guidance did not map cleanly to contextual questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Search and configurable language checks cover routine lookups. A bounded model can connect a passage to retrieved guidance while exposing its sources.
tasks.still_hard: Dialect, intentional voice, multilingual usage, and conflicting reference editions require judgement. Reference licences may restrict indexing.
tasks.human_edge: The proofreader distinguishes an actual error from a deliberate stylistic choice.

ambition.what: A cited language-query desk for marketing writers.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding reference entries, and more goes into difficult language questions. The proofreader gains no new authority over substantive editorial changes.

reach.task: Resolve multilingual terminology and usage queries.
reach.learn: Learn locale conventions, terminology governance, and when a native-language specialist is needed.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling checks and reference lookup can handle defined terms; contextual grammar recommendations still require validation.
The digest provides no documented case establishing proofreading accuracy or savings for this design.

tasks.statement: Consult reference books or secure aid of readers to check references with rules of grammar and composition.

tasks.short: Route marked proofs to the right people and track their return.

steps.what: Check that marked proofs match the current manuscript and include all correction pages.
Identify the correction owner and deadline from the production schedule.
Send marked proofs and correction instructions to the assigned author, editor, or typesetter.
Record dispatch, check acknowledgement, and chase overdue corrected proofs.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} to route versioned proofs from the {DOCS}, with a deterministic check for document identity and package completeness. The proofreader approves dispatch to external recipients through the {EMAIL}; acknowledgement tracking and fixed reminders then run automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proof versions, recipient details, and deadlines were scattered across files and correspondence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow configuration handles assignment and reminders. AI coding reduces the effort of adding file checks and connecting records.
tasks.still_hard: Scanned handwritten marks, missing ownership, and proofs returned outside the agreed channel still create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The proofreader recognises when a correction needs an editor's decision rather than another production pass.

ambition.what: A correction handoff service with a visible return deadline for each proof.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer dispatches and chasers, with more time for stalled or ambiguous corrections. Editorial and print-release decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Learn file dependencies, layout version identifiers, and which changes require a fresh proof.

evidence.claim: Version checks, owner mappings, dispatch records, and scheduled reminders can use deterministic workflows.

The typical workflow includes an external production recipient; dispatch approval applies to that disclosure.
Automatic reminders use fixed text, the approved recipient, and a capped schedule.
Dispatch requests corrections; it does not authorise printing or additional expenditure.
Build ranges cover one team and one proof route; access and consultation elapsed time may be longer.

Whether recipient ownership and deadlines exist in structured records.
Which recipients are external and which documents they may receive.

tasks.statement: Route proofs with marked corrections to authors, editors, typists, or typesetters for correction or reprinting.

tasks.short: Read proofs aloud so a second checker can catch text and punctuation differences.

steps.what: Retrieve matching versions of approved copy and proof sheets.
Read proof aloud, naming punctuation and spelling unusual words and proper names.
Follow the spoken proof against approved copy and mark discrepancies.
Resolve disputed names, punctuation and intentional differences.
Record agreed corrections and send them for implementation.

tasks.design: A deterministic comparison job retrieves paired versions from {DOCS}, checks text and punctuation, and creates page-linked differences for review. This removes routine paired reading for eligible digital proofs; {WORKFLOW} records approved corrections and routes them to the desktop publisher, while specialist or unreliable inputs retain human checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paired reading bridged paper proofs, unreliable extraction and weak version control. Digital comparison was already possible but often disconnected from the correction workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable version identifiers, direct text extraction and inexpensive comparison workflows make routine checks easier to connect. A model loop is unnecessary for exact textual fidelity.
tasks.still_hard: Columns, ligatures, outlined text and scans can break extraction or reading order. Names need authoritative references, and tactile braille or physical output needs specialist checks.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a real error from an intended change and recognising when the source itself is wrong.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer paired reading sessions and more review of meaningful differences. No new editorial decision rights are created.

reach.task: Check terminology and proper-name consistency across a document set.
reach.learn: Terminology management, authoritative references and controlled document versions.

evidence.claim: Exact digital text comparison can replace oral comparison when source pairing and extraction are reliable.
A study documented invented phrases in speech-to-text output.
The digest provides no direct case measuring the replacement of paired proof reading.
Time allocations, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

tasks.short: Discuss proposed manuscript corrections with authors and editors and record agreed changes.

steps.what: Gather disputed passages, correction suggestions, and supporting references for discussion.

loop.input: Marked passages, proposed corrections, available reference advice, and the current manuscript.
loop.output: A brief grouping open questions with passage links and alternative wording.
loop.check: Require a source passage for every question; compare quoted wording with the current manuscript.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unreadable marks or uncertain intent remain explicit open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Grouping overlapping free-text comments and expressing their differences needs limited language interpretation.

steps.what: Discuss intended meaning, explain corrections, and explore wording with the author and editor.
Approve the chosen wording or defer the question for further advice.
Record agreed changes and assign unresolved questions to their owners.

tasks.design: Generate a source-linked discussion brief from comments in the {DOCS}, using a bounded drafting loop. Authors, editors, and proofreaders discuss the wording; an explicit editorial decision then creates correction instructions and follow-up records in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Discussion preparation required reading scattered comments, and meeting decisions were recorded inconsistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Document comments can feed a brief generator. Structured decision capture lets existing workflows create follow-up records without interpreting a meeting transcript.
tasks.still_hard: Creative intent, disagreement, and trust remain human work. A concise brief can still hide an important nuance unless reviewed.
tasks.human_edge: The proofreader explains an error tactfully and helps the author preserve the intended meaning.

reach.learn: Learn editorial scope, author intent, and how to separate correction from rewriting.

tasks.short: Read copy, research supporting information, and archive the document record.

steps.what: Locate the current copy, assignment brief, and relevant earlier versions.
Read the copy for context and note names, references, or statements needing research.

loop.input: Current copy and assignment brief, divided into fixed sections.
loop.output: Passage-linked names, references, and potentially checkable statements.
loop.check: Require exact source spans, process every section, and have the proofreader check coverage.
loop.stop: One pass per section and one repair for invalid spans; unsupported or unreadable sections go to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Recognising implied references and context-dependent statements requires reading free text.

steps.what: Search approved references and public websites for relevant information.
Check source relevance and currency, then record evidence and unresolved questions.
Archive copy and research notes with version, assignment, and retention metadata.

A bounded reader proposes a passage-linked research list; configured search helps the proofreader find sources, while the proofreader evaluates evidence and refers substantive issues to the editor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading, public research, and filing were treated as one activity, although only parts followed stable rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Document metadata and search already support retrieval and filing. A bounded reading pass can prepare research questions without attempting open-ended autonomous research.
tasks.still_hard: Sources can be outdated, contradictory, inaccessible, or unsuitable for the claim. Contextual reading cannot safely be reduced to extracting named entities.
tasks.human_edge: The proofreader notices missing context and recognises when evidence does not support the wording.

tasks.short: Write headlines, captions, cutlines and cover copy from an approved brief.

loop.input: Copy brief, source pack and style guide.
loop.output: Requirements with source references and unresolved questions.

loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unresolved requirements go to the proofreader.

loop.stop: One batch and one requested revision; unsatisfactory results return to manual writing.

steps.what: Check spelling, punctuation, length and required wording.
Resolve factual, tonal and contextual issues and select the preferred wording.
Approve wording for its intended audience and use.
Place approved wording in the publication draft.
